mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate relative to its long-term average compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% over the past month signals strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer demand and labor market strength, which together drive positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS growth and PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE >= 6.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as economic weakness weighs on corporate earnings, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is >=6.0%, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (INDPRO) above 115.0 indicates a strengthening manufacturing sector, which supports corporate profit growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is above 115.0.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 345,000 million dollars, it signals robust consumer spending that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 345000, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 100,000) indicates a supportive monetary policy and labor market, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and PAYEMS > 100000 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2.5%, it indicates an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity market gains, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.5%.
